issue.title: task_type completion offers #<type> on a body-less project-note item (@route^id@ #f) that capture refuses

task_type_fields.impact: Bob Mac Capture's Task type menu shows FIX/BUILD/... as acceptable on a new project-note draft; accepting and capturing then fails with type_marker_not_applicable, so the menu disagrees with capture until a title is typed.
task_type_fields.repro:
Reproduced with installed bob 0.6.0 against the live vault config (FIX configured):

```sh
bob capture-complete --all-tasks --cursor 13 --format json -- '@dev^foo@ #f'
# task_type, subject new, FIX row: replacement "#fix ", refused: null
bob capture --dry-run --format json -- '@dev^foo@ #fix Fix it'
# {"code":"type_marker_not_applicable","error":"... this capture creates a project note; set `task_type:` in the new note","ok":false}
```

Root cause: `subject_refusal` (src/native/capture_complete/task_types.rs) probes the draft with `#bob-type` and refuses only when `parse_for_editor` reports `type_marker_not_applicable` for the item. For a body-less project-note item (`@dev^foo@ #bob-type`) the editor parse reports only `type_marker_needs_task`; it reports `type_marker_not_applicable` once a body exists (`bob capture-parse -- '@dev^foo@ #fix Fix '` → mode project_note with type_marker_not_applicable). So completion's refusal depends on whether a title has been typed yet, while capture always refuses.

Fix direction: make the editor parse report `type_marker_not_applicable` for a type marker on a project-note (and other non-task) item regardless of body, or make `subject_refusal` probe with a placeholder body; add a `complete_task_types.rs` test that `@route^id@ #f` rows carry `refused: "type_marker_not_applicable"`.
